character_facts: Aghora was turned into a heavily augmented living weapon through years of painful operations.
Aghora's father directs or assigns her early super-mercenary work.
Aghora's first assignment is as an executioner rather than a conventional battlefield mission.
Aghora is portrayed as disciplined or being taught discipline in lethal combat situations.
Algholkar of Rieidar is presented as a notoriously hard-to-kill opponent.
continuity_links: This page functions as backstory for Aghora, explaining how she was weaponized and what kind of work defined her early career.
The narration connects Aghora's implanted arsenal to her later effectiveness as an executioner of extreme prisoners.
The mention of her father establishes his controlling role in shaping her training and assignments.
dialogue_meaning: The narration explains that Aghora was deliberately weaponized through extensive surgical augmentation.
It frames her first major role as galaxy-wide executioner duty on Khaliyuga, emphasizing the cruelty and scale of the work.
It states that her routine involved killing vast numbers of condemned prisoners over multiple years.
The speech bubble conveys a combat lesson: against deadly attacks such as acid jets, one must maintain total focus in the present moment.
lore_facts: Aghora had Oko mini-bombs implanted inside her body.
Aghora also received multiple other internal weapons said to be capable of enormous destruction.
Khaliyuga is a prison planet where condemned beings are brought for execution.
Prisoner convoys arrive from across the galaxy.
Some condemned prisoners belong to species that are difficult to kill.
Aghora's execution rate is stated as 200 prisoners per day for three years.
Algholkar is from Rieidar and is considered one of the difficult or nearly unbeatable prisoners.
plot_events: Over several years, Aghora undergoes repeated painful operations to have a network of Oko mini-bombs and other weapons implanted in her body.
Aghora receives her first assignment as a super-mercenary from her father.
She is assigned to serve as executioner on the prison planet Khaliyuga.
Convoys continually deliver condemned beings from across the galaxy to Khaliyuga for execution.
For three years, Aghora kills 200 prisoners per day.
One highlighted prisoner is Algholkar of Rieidar, described as especially hard to defeat.
During a confrontation with a creature that uses acid jets, someone instructs that survival depends on constant focus.
uncertainties: Some proper nouns are difficult to read with full certainty, especially 'Oko,' 'Khaliyuga,' 'Algholkar,' and 'Rieidar.'
The speaker of the combat advice in the final panel is not visually identified on this page.
The exact identity of the small airborne figure in the last panel is unclear from the image alone.
visual_summary: Narration boxes describe Aghora’s transformation and early career while the art shows invasive surgery and mass execution. In the top panels, a bald young Aghora lies restrained as tubes, drills, and mechanical arms implant weapons into her body. The middle panel shifts to space, with armed convoys approaching a large prison-world or station. The bottom panel shows a huge armored spherical prisoner or beast spraying corrosive jets while armed figures surround it, and a small airborne figure appears to evade the attack as a speech bubble offers combat instruction.
